- AGENT UX LAYER GAPS (orchestrator review). The plan currently treats agent UX as deliverables-to-land rather than a UX surface to design. Add an explicit '## Agent UX Surface' subsection to the sprint plan with day-tagged commitments addressing all of the following:

1) TIERED NOTICE/WARN DISCIPLINE. SD-018 names three tiers (info / notice / warn) but the plan must commit to firing rules: Info = every run; Notice = first run of process, gap >1h, cwd change, auto-reopen of archived thread; Warn = brief-novelty against thread history (parsable, rare). Acceptance criterion: 'Warn tier fires <5% of runs in dogfood or the trigger thresholds get tuned before Day 10.' Without this discipline the implementation drifts into warning-spam and agents learn to ignore the lines.

2) [HINT] LINE for suspected manual fan-out (3+ sequential runs of the same executor with no --variants flag) suggesting 'thread group <ids>'. Schedule on Day 4 alongside the [variants] nag. Soft nudge, not warning.

3) [THREAD-HEALTH] SMELL LINE on 'thread list' output (e.g., '12 variant groups, 0 kept' or '3 open threads idle >5d'). Schedule Day 3 with the lifecycle CLI.

4) SKILL.MD ONE-SENTENCE WORDING IS LOAD-BEARING. Every agent will pattern off it. The plan must specify the exact text to land on Day 3, not 'add a paragraph'. Suggested anchor: 'At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new.' Plan can refine but must commit to the exact wording.

5) OUTPUT-FORMAT STABILITY COMMITMENT. The [thread] and [variants] prefix lines are part of the public CLI contract. Add to Definition of Done: 'prefix line format governed by schema_version; format changes require a major version bump and a transition period.' Agents that pattern-match break silently otherwise.

6) LINE-ORDERING RULE when [thread], [variants], Notice, and Warn all fire on the same run. Specify: stream (stdout for all, before any other output); order (thread, variants, notice, warn, then command output); separator (single blank line between prefix block and command output). Trivial to specify on Day 2, expensive to fix later.

7) ITERATION_VIDEO INSPECT AS PRIMARY DISCOVERY TOOL. The plan treats it as one subcommand among five but it is THE gesture an agent should run before any iteration-video render (per the design's agent-UX reasoning). The SKILL.md text or a separate iteration-video doc must instruct: 'Always run iteration_video inspect <thread> before iteration_video run; it shows detected modalities, chosen renderers, estimated cost, and quality score so you can adjust before committing to a render.'

8) COST ESTIMATE SURFACING per SD-043. iteration_video inspect must print estimated cost (= summarize_calls * model_cost + render_cost_estimate) BEFORE the agent commits to a render. Schedule on Day 6 with iteration.collect (which has the run count) or Day 9 with the orchestrator wiring. Acceptance: 'inspect output includes a Cost section with low/high range and a one-line recommendation.'

9) THE FAILURE-MODE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (most important). An agent that forgets threads exist will silently lump everything into one giant pile and the killer demo dies. Add to Day 10 dogfood acceptance: 'verify that during dogfood the [thread] prefix appeared on the stdout of every executors run / orchestrators run invocation, that thread show @active was called by the agent before iteration_video, and that no run was attributed to thread @active when a more recent thread had been opened (lineage inference worked).' Make it observable, not assumed.

10) DOCUMENT WHEN EACH TIER FIRES in docs/threads.md so agents reading the doc can predict what they'll see. Day 5 deliverable, scoped to one short table.

These items are load-bearing for adoption: if the agent UX is sloppy, the data the iteration video reads is sloppy, and the demo lies. They are not deferrable to a follow-up sprint.

Prior doc imported via --from-doc:
docs/design-thread-layer.md
Imported decisions (from the source doc's ## Settled Decisions section): 40
Imported decision details:
- SD-001: Use the noun `thread` for a creative pursuit, not `workstream`/`session`/`pursuit`. The name appears in every `[thread]` prefix line and must match the creator's mental model
  rationale: chosen after explicit subagent debate; matches creator language ("pull on this thread"); short to type; the git overload is tolerable in the creative-tools domain.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-002: Tags-not-folders: every run writes a `runs/<slug>/run.json` with a `thread_id` field. The `runs/` directory stays flat. Re-grouping (split/merge/attach) is a metadata edit, never a `mv` operation
  rationale: coupling physical layout to logical grouping makes re-attribution destructive and breaks path references in older timelines. Identity is by ULID, never by path.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-003: A single index file `.artagents/threads.json` holds the thread map and `active_thread_id` pointer. All updates go through `fcntl.flock` on a sidecar lock file plus atomic write (tmp + fsync + `os.replace`), with a rotated `.bak`
  rationale: parallel runs must not lose updates; the index is small enough that single-file is correct.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-004: IDs are 26-char Crockford ULIDs (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `group_id`), monotonic within a process. References between records are always by ULID, never by path or label
  rationale: lex-sortable, stable across renames, no central registry needed.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-005: `parent_run_ids` on a run is **plural and causal**, derived from input-artifact hashes against producer `run_id`s — not the temporal previous run in the thread. A run with no consumed artifacts has empty `parent_run_ids` (it is a root)
  rationale: temporal parentage lies during interleaved work; causal parentage is reconstructible and honest.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-006: Auto-attribute decision function, evaluated at run start under the lock:
  rationale: lineage inference is the highest-ROI auto-attribution improvement; it removes a whole class of mis-grouping when the agent works across shells.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-007: Thread lifecycle: `open → archived → (re)open`. Archive triggers are explicit command, successful export/publish, or idle ≥ `IDLE_ARCHIVE_WINDOW` (default 7d). Reopen triggers are explicit command or new run within `IDLE_REOPEN_WINDOW`. Lazy enforcement on read; no daemon
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-008: `run.json` schema (frozen for v1 of the layer). Required fields:
  rationale: this is the irreversible part. Every run produced after sprint day 1 either has these fields or doesn't, forever. Metadata can be collected now and used by deferred features later.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-009: Brief snapshotting: every run writes `runs/<slug>/brief.copy.txt` and stamps `brief_content_sha256` in `run.json`. Briefs get edited in place between runs; without snapshotting, prompt diffs in the iteration video are unreconstructable
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-010: `external_service_calls` captures `model` and `model_version` per call, plus `seed`, `cost_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `request_id` where available. Models drift (gpt-image-1 → gpt-image-2 produces different outputs); `agent_version` (toolkit git sha) is insufficient on its own. `request_id` lets deleted external artifacts be re-fetched
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-011: `input_artifacts` records `produced_by_run_id` at the moment of consumption (computed from artifact sha256 against known runs). Without this, the causal DAG must be reconstructed later from hashes — possible but expensive and broken if intermediate runs are deleted
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-012: `host_id` = `sha256(hostname:user)[:16]`. Captured per run for provenance only. Not used for tracking, not transmitted. Lets a future sync tool reconcile cross-machine threads
  rationale: cheap to capture, expensive to add later if missed.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-013: Variants primitive: extend each `output_artifact` with `role` (`variant`/`ancillary`/`manifest`/`index`), `group` (= `sha256(run_id + group_label)[:16]`), `group_index`, and a free-form `variant_meta` blob. **Default role is `ancillary`. Executors must opt in to `variant`. Fail closed.**
  rationale: heterogeneous outputs (4 candidates + grid + manifest) cannot accidentally poison the variant group; executors that produce siblings declare them explicitly.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-014: Selection state lives at the thread, not the artifact. An append-only `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/selections.jsonl` records each `{ts, group, kept[], discarded[], by, note?}` event. Never mutated. Current-keepers reduces over the log
  rationale: handles partial selection, deselection, and revision without losing history; concurrent picks are safe (last write wins on read).
  load_bearing: True
- SD-015: `chosen_from_groups: [{group, sha256}]` on a consuming run is a **separate edge** from `parent_run_ids`. The DAG distinguishes "descended from X" (causal) from "picked over its siblings" (curatorial). The iteration video needs both
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-016: Denormalized `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/groups.json` index gives O(1) lookups for "what variants for run #N, which kept, which descended." Updated on run-write and selection-write
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-017: Agent gesture surface for variants — exactly five commands, one of which is mandatory-per-attempt:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-018: Runner-emitted prefix lines on every `executors run` and `orchestrators run` invocation, written to stdout BEFORE the rest of the command output (so the agent sees them in tool result):
  rationale: the agent's working memory is the previous tool's stdout; thread state must be in that stream every turn.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-019: Provenance block in `hype.metadata.json` (added to `pipeline` block by `builtin.cut`). Carries `{thread_id, thread_label (denormalized), run_id, parent_run_ids[], chosen_from_groups[], contributing_runs[{run_id, thread_id, artifact_path, sha256}], starred, agent_version}`. Denormalization of `thread_label` and `agent_version` makes the artifact self-contained after `rm -rf .artagents/`
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-020: `builtin.iteration_video` is a single orchestrator polymorphic across modalities, not per-modality orchestrators. Real threads are heterogeneous (storyboard → animation, music video) and the agent shouldn't have to pick a modality before knowing what's in the thread
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-021: Iteration-video executor chain: `iteration.collect` → `iteration.summarize` (calls `builtin.understand` in parallel) → `iteration.score` → `iteration.assemble` → `builtin.cut` → `builtin.render`. Three new executors; the rest are reused. `iteration.assemble` is the only piece with non-trivial new visual logic
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-022: Iteration-video outputs (a single variant group):
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-023: Default ancestry is `provenance-graph` (walk `parent_run_ids` backward from target), not `thread`. Threads are a human construct that drift; causal parentage is hash-derived and doesn't lie. The HTML report labels which runs were "in-thread" vs "pulled in by ancestry."
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-024: Quality floor: `iteration.collect` computes a `data_quality` score in [0,1]. If below `quality_floor` (default 0.6), the orchestrator **refuses to render** and emits an actionable report listing the specific runs missing `parent_run_ids` with exact backfill commands. `--force` bypasses, logged into provenance
  rationale: silently rendering a video that misorders or omits half the runs destroys trust permanently. Refusal must be a helpful editor, not a bureaucrat.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-025: `ModalityRenderer` registry at `artagents/modalities/` (sibling to `elements/`, `executors/`, `orchestrators/`). Each renderer is a small declarative file declaring `kinds`, `clip_modes`, `default_clip_mode_for(shape, style)`, `produces_audio`, `cost_hint`. Discoverable via `python3 -m artagents modalities {list, inspect}`
  rationale: replaces a hardcoded global decision table that would become unmaintainable as modalities multiply. Each renderer owns its own scoped logic.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-026: Capability declarations on artifacts: extend `output_artifacts` with `preview_modes: [...]` and `duration` (where applicable). Producers declare what previews are tractable. The renderer registry resolves `(kind, preview_modes)` to a renderer at assembly time
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-027: Agent surface for iteration video — five flags + one inspect command total:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-028: Audio-bed automatic selection: if `produces_audio` renderers cover >40% of clip duration → iterations-as-bed (cross-fade between audio variants). Else theme-declared bed. Else silence + subtle room tone. **Never generative music** — ages badly, fights the content
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-029: `generic_card` renderer is always registered as a fallback. When it fires, every iteration that uses it gets a "no renderer for `kind:<X>`" annotation in the HTML report and a stdout warning. Unknown modalities degrade gracefully and **loudly**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-030: Single chokepoint integration: `run_executor()` at `artagents/executors/runner.py:75` and the orchestrator-runner equivalent are wrapped with `threads.begin(request)` / `threads.finalize(record_id, result)`. The wrapper is a no-op when: `dry_run=True`, `request.out` is unwritable or under `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `request.thread == "@none"`, or env `ARTAGENTS_THREADS_OFF=1` is set. **No executor's `run.py` is modified except where it produces variant outputs.**

No other executor `run.py` is modified.\n+\n+### Week 2: Iteration Video MVP\n+\n+- **Day 6** lands SD-023, SD-024, SD-025, and the first v1 half of SD-021: modality registry, exactly three renderers, provenance-graph collection, and `data_quality` inside `iteration.prepare`.\n+- **Day 6** also starts SD-043 inside `iteration.prepare`: count candidate runs before dispatch, honor `max_iterations`, and prepare cache keys.\n+- **Day 7** completes the SD-021 `iteration.prepare` work: summarization through `builtin.understand`, scoring, cache writes, cost-cap refusal, and deterministic ordering.\n+- **Day 8** lands SD-026, SD-027, SD-028, and SD-029 inside `iteration.assemble`: v1 kind-based renderer dispatch, direction as label-only, chaptered mode only, automatic audio-bed selection, and loud `generic_card` fallback.\n+- **Day 9** lands SD-020, SD-022, and the orchestrator surface of SD-043: `builtin.iteration_video`, the five output artifacts, `iteration_video inspect`, estimated cost, and `--no-content` report behavior.\n+- **Day 10** lands SD-035 acceptance: dogfood against `runs/artagents_logo_v3`, full integration pass, 60-second demo render, and observable failure-mode checks.\n+- **Sprint cuts**: SD-036 remains out of scope in full, and DEF-1 through DEF-10 are explicitly not implemented in this sprint.\n+\n+## Open Question Resolutions\n+\n+- **OQ-1: Day-by-day allocation.** Resolved by the Week 1 and Week 2 sections: Days 1-5 are data, Days 6-10 are iteration video, with Day 2 as the schema freeze and Day 10 as the demo gate.\n+- **OQ-2: Summarization parallelism.** Use `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=int(os.environ.get(\"ARTAGENTS_SUMMARIZE_CONCURRENCY\", \"4\")))` inside the summarize phase of `iteration.prepare`, with exponential backoff per `builtin.understand` call. Keep `ARTAGENTS_SUMMARIZE_SEQUENTIAL=1` as an implementation/debug fallback if rate limits or local determinism require it.\n+- **OQ-3: Prefix format.** Width is `min(120, $COLUMNS)` when `$COLUMNS` is available, otherwise 120. ANSI color is allowed only when stdout is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is unset. Labels truncate to 32 display characters; IDs are never truncated. All prefix lines stream to stdout before command output. V1 order is `[thread] -> [variants] -> Notice: -> blank line -> command output`; `[hint]` and `Warn:` are deferred by DEF-3 and DEF-1. Format stability is governed by `schema_version` and the Definition of Done.\n+- **OQ-4: Reaper timing.** Run the SD-033 in-flight reaper lazily on first index read per process. It is not a daemon and not a per-command directory walk after the first read.\n+- **OQ-5: Global documentation location.** Use `docs/threads.md` for the long-form reference. Day 3 lands a short stub explaining the prefix; Day 5 expands privacy, selection semantics, tier firing rules, inspect-before-render, and deferred features.\n+- **OQ-6: Quality floor formula.** `data_quality = 0.5*parent_capture_score + 0.3*has_brief_sha + 0.2*has_resolved_input_artifact`, where `parent_capture_score = (runs_with_parents + valid_roots)/total_runs` and `valid_root iff input_artifacts==[]`. The floor is 0.6. Refusal reports name only unresolved-producer runs; valid roots are not penalized and are never listed as missing lineage.\n*** End Patch\n"

        Prior doc context:
Prior doc imported via --from-doc:
docs/design-thread-layer.md
Imported decisions (from the source doc's ## Settled Decisions section): 40
Imported decision details:
- SD-001: Use the noun `thread` for a creative pursuit, not `workstream`/`session`/`pursuit`. The name appears in every `[thread]` prefix line and must match the creator's mental model
  rationale: chosen after explicit subagent debate; matches creator language ("pull on this thread"); short to type; the git overload is tolerable in the creative-tools domain.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-002: Tags-not-folders: every run writes a `runs/<slug>/run.json` with a `thread_id` field. The `runs/` directory stays flat. Re-grouping (split/merge/attach) is a metadata edit, never a `mv` operation
  rationale: coupling physical layout to logical grouping makes re-attribution destructive and breaks path references in older timelines. Identity is by ULID, never by path.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-003: A single index file `.artagents/threads.json` holds the thread map and `active_thread_id` pointer. All updates go through `fcntl.flock` on a sidecar lock file plus atomic write (tmp + fsync + `os.replace`), with a rotated `.bak`
  rationale: parallel runs must not lose updates; the index is small enough that single-file is correct.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-004: IDs are 26-char Crockford ULIDs (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `group_id`), monotonic within a process. References between records are always by ULID, never by path or label
  rationale: lex-sortable, stable across renames, no central registry needed.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-005: `parent_run_ids` on a run is **plural and causal**, derived from input-artifact hashes against producer `run_id`s — not the temporal previous run in the thread. A run with no consumed artifacts has empty `parent_run_ids` (it is a root)
  rationale: temporal parentage lies during interleaved work; causal parentage is reconstructible and honest.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-006: Auto-attribute decision function, evaluated at run start under the lock:
  rationale: lineage inference is the highest-ROI auto-attribution improvement; it removes a whole class of mis-grouping when the agent works across shells.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-007: Thread lifecycle: `open → archived → (re)open`. Archive triggers are explicit command, successful export/publish, or idle ≥ `IDLE_ARCHIVE_WINDOW` (default 7d). Reopen triggers are explicit command or new run within `IDLE_REOPEN_WINDOW`. Lazy enforcement on read; no daemon
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-008: `run.json` schema (frozen for v1 of the layer). Required fields:
  rationale: this is the irreversible part. Every run produced after sprint day 1 either has these fields or doesn't, forever. Metadata can be collected now and used by deferred features later.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-009: Brief snapshotting: every run writes `runs/<slug>/brief.copy.txt` and stamps `brief_content_sha256` in `run.json`. Briefs get edited in place between runs; without snapshotting, prompt diffs in the iteration video are unreconstructable
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-010: `external_service_calls` captures `model` and `model_version` per call, plus `seed`, `cost_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `request_id` where available. Models drift (gpt-image-1 → gpt-image-2 produces different outputs); `agent_version` (toolkit git sha) is insufficient on its own. `request_id` lets deleted external artifacts be re-fetched
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-011: `input_artifacts` records `produced_by_run_id` at the moment of consumption (computed from artifact sha256 against known runs). Without this, the causal DAG must be reconstructed later from hashes — possible but expensive and broken if intermediate runs are deleted
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-012: `host_id` = `sha256(hostname:user)[:16]`. Captured per run for provenance only. Not used for tracking, not transmitted. Lets a future sync tool reconcile cross-machine threads
  rationale: cheap to capture, expensive to add later if missed.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-013: Variants primitive: extend each `output_artifact` with `role` (`variant`/`ancillary`/`manifest`/`index`), `group` (= `sha256(run_id + group_label)[:16]`), `group_index`, and a free-form `variant_meta` blob. **Default role is `ancillary`. Executors must opt in to `variant`. Fail closed.**
  rationale: heterogeneous outputs (4 candidates + grid + manifest) cannot accidentally poison the variant group; executors that produce siblings declare them explicitly.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-014: Selection state lives at the thread, not the artifact. An append-only `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/selections.jsonl` records each `{ts, group, kept[], discarded[], by, note?}` event. Never mutated. Current-keepers reduces over the log
  rationale: handles partial selection, deselection, and revision without losing history; concurrent picks are safe (last write wins on read).
  load_bearing: True
- SD-015: `chosen_from_groups: [{group, sha256}]` on a consuming run is a **separate edge** from `parent_run_ids`. The DAG distinguishes "descended from X" (causal) from "picked over its siblings" (curatorial). The iteration video needs both
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-016: Denormalized `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/groups.json` index gives O(1) lookups for "what variants for run #N, which kept, which descended." Updated on run-write and selection-write
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-017: Agent gesture surface for variants — exactly five commands, one of which is mandatory-per-attempt:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-018: Runner-emitted prefix lines on every `executors run` and `orchestrators run` invocation, written to stdout BEFORE the rest of the command output (so the agent sees them in tool result):
  rationale: the agent's working memory is the previous tool's stdout; thread state must be in that stream every turn.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-019: Provenance block in `hype.metadata.json` (added to `pipeline` block by `builtin.cut`). Carries `{thread_id, thread_label (denormalized), run_id, parent_run_ids[], chosen_from_groups[], contributing_runs[{run_id, thread_id, artifact_path, sha256}], starred, agent_version}`. Denormalization of `thread_label` and `agent_version` makes the artifact self-contained after `rm -rf .artagents/`
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-020: `builtin.iteration_video` is a single orchestrator polymorphic across modalities, not per-modality orchestrators. Real threads are heterogeneous (storyboard → animation, music video) and the agent shouldn't have to pick a modality before knowing what's in the thread
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-021: Iteration-video executor chain: `iteration.collect` → `iteration.summarize` (calls `builtin.understand` in parallel) → `iteration.score` → `iteration.assemble` → `builtin.cut` → `builtin.render`. Three new executors; the rest are reused. `iteration.assemble` is the only piece with non-trivial new visual logic
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-022: Iteration-video outputs (a single variant group):
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-023: Default ancestry is `provenance-graph` (walk `parent_run_ids` backward from target), not `thread`. Threads are a human construct that drift; causal parentage is hash-derived and doesn't lie. The HTML report labels which runs were "in-thread" vs "pulled in by ancestry."
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-024: Quality floor: `iteration.collect` computes a `data_quality` score in [0,1]. If below `quality_floor` (default 0.6), the orchestrator **refuses to render** and emits an actionable report listing the specific runs missing `parent_run_ids` with exact backfill commands. `--force` bypasses, logged into provenance
  rationale: silently rendering a video that misorders or omits half the runs destroys trust permanently. Refusal must be a helpful editor, not a bureaucrat.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-025: `ModalityRenderer` registry at `artagents/modalities/` (sibling to `elements/`, `executors/`, `orchestrators/`). Each renderer is a small declarative file declaring `kinds`, `clip_modes`, `default_clip_mode_for(shape, style)`, `produces_audio`, `cost_hint`. Discoverable via `python3 -m artagents modalities {list, inspect}`
  rationale: replaces a hardcoded global decision table that would become unmaintainable as modalities multiply. Each renderer owns its own scoped logic.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-026: Capability declarations on artifacts: extend `output_artifacts` with `preview_modes: [...]` and `duration` (where applicable). Producers declare what previews are tractable. The renderer registry resolves `(kind, preview_modes)` to a renderer at assembly time
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-027: Agent surface for iteration video — five flags + one inspect command total:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-028: Audio-bed automatic selection: if `produces_audio` renderers cover >40% of clip duration → iterations-as-bed (cross-fade between audio variants). Else theme-declared bed. Else silence + subtle room tone. **Never generative music** — ages badly, fights the content
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-029: `generic_card` renderer is always registered as a fallback. When it fires, every iteration that uses it gets a "no renderer for `kind:<X>`" annotation in the HTML report and a stdout warning. Unknown modalities degrade gracefully and **loudly**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-030: Single chokepoint integration: `run_executor()` at `artagents/executors/runner.py:75` and the orchestrator-runner equivalent are wrapped with `threads.begin(request)` / `threads.finalize(record_id, result)`. The wrapper is a no-op when: `dry_run=True`, `request.out` is unwritable or under `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `request.thread == "@none"`, or env `ARTAGENTS_THREADS_OFF=1` is set. **No executor's `run.py` is modified except where it produces variant outputs.**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-031: Existing-executor patches required by this layer:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-032: Hashing strategy: `xxhash` for `inputs_digest` (fast, non-cryptographic, used for dedup detection only). `sha256` for `output_artifacts[*].sha256` (one-shot at run end, never blocking the runner mid-run). Multi-GB renders must not block
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-033: In-flight reaper: any run start scans `runs/*/run.json` for records with `ended_at: null` whose owning process is gone (PID stamped at begin). Marks them `returncode: -1, ended_at: <now>, status: "orphaned"`. Lazy, runs at most once per process
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-034: Backwards compatibility is mandatory. Existing `runs/*/` directories without `run.json` continue to work unmodified. `python3 -m artagents thread backfill` scans, computes hashes, and adopts orphan dirs into auto-named threads (clustered by hash-graph connected components, not mtime). All existing tests must pass without modification
  rationale:

- SD-035: Sprint phasing constraints (load-bearing for the planner):

- SD-036: Sprint cuts (explicitly out of scope for the 2-week sprint, deferred to follow-up):

  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-039: Schema versioning: `run.json`, `threads.json`, `selections.jsonl`, `groups.json`, and the `provenance` block all carry `schema_version: int`. Readers accept current and N-1; writers always write current; one-time migration runs on first read at upgrade time, with `.bak`
  rationale:

- SD-040: All paths in persisted JSON are repo-relative or content-addressed. No absolute paths. This makes thread export/sharing (a future feature) work for free as long as we hold the line now

Prior doc imported via --from-doc:
docs/design-thread-layer.md
Imported decisions (from the source doc's ## Settled Decisions section): 40
Imported decision details:
- SD-001: Use the noun `thread` for a creative pursuit, not `workstream`/`session`/`pursuit`. The name appears in every `[thread]` prefix line and must match the creator's mental model
  rationale: chosen after explicit subagent debate; matches creator language ("pull on this thread"); short to type; the git overload is tolerable in the creative-tools domain.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-002: Tags-not-folders: every run writes a `runs/<slug>/run.json` with a `thread_id` field. The `runs/` directory stays flat. Re-grouping (split/merge/attach) is a metadata edit, never a `mv` operation
  rationale: coupling physical layout to logical grouping makes re-attribution destructive and breaks path references in older timelines. Identity is by ULID, never by path.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-003: A single index file `.artagents/threads.json` holds the thread map and `active_thread_id` pointer. All updates go through `fcntl.flock` on a sidecar lock file plus atomic write (tmp + fsync + `os.replace`), with a rotated `.bak`
  rationale: parallel runs must not lose updates; the index is small enough that single-file is correct.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-004: IDs are 26-char Crockford ULIDs (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `group_id`), monotonic within a process. References between records are always by ULID, never by path or label
  rationale: lex-sortable, stable across renames, no central registry needed.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-005: `parent_run_ids` on a run is **plural and causal**, derived from input-artifact hashes against producer `run_id`s — not the temporal previous run in the thread. A run with no consumed artifacts has empty `parent_run_ids` (it is a root)
  rationale: temporal parentage lies during interleaved work; causal parentage is reconstructible and honest.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-006: Auto-attribute decision function, evaluated at run start under the lock:
  rationale: lineage inference is the highest-ROI auto-attribution improvement; it removes a whole class of mis-grouping when the agent works across shells.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-007: Thread lifecycle: `open → archived → (re)open`. Archive triggers are explicit command, successful export/publish, or idle ≥ `IDLE_ARCHIVE_WINDOW` (default 7d). Reopen triggers are explicit command or new run within `IDLE_REOPEN_WINDOW`. Lazy enforcement on read; no daemon
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-008: `run.json` schema (frozen for v1 of the layer). Required fields:
  rationale: this is the irreversible part. Every run produced after sprint day 1 either has these fields or doesn't, forever. Metadata can be collected now and used by deferred features later.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-009: Brief snapshotting: every run writes `runs/<slug>/brief.copy.txt` and stamps `brief_content_sha256` in `run.json`. Briefs get edited in place between runs; without snapshotting, prompt diffs in the iteration video are unreconstructable
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-010: `external_service_calls` captures `model` and `model_version` per call, plus `seed`, `cost_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `request_id` where available. Models drift (gpt-image-1 → gpt-image-2 produces different outputs); `agent_version` (toolkit git sha) is insufficient on its own. `request_id` lets deleted external artifacts be re-fetched
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-011: `input_artifacts` records `produced_by_run_id` at the moment of consumption (computed from artifact sha256 against known runs). Without this, the causal DAG must be reconstructed later from hashes — possible but expensive and broken if intermediate runs are deleted
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-012: `host_id` = `sha256(hostname:user)[:16]`. Captured per run for provenance only. Not used for tracking, not transmitted. Lets a future sync tool reconcile cross-machine threads
  rationale: cheap to capture, expensive to add later if missed.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-013: Variants primitive: extend each `output_artifact` with `role` (`variant`/`ancillary`/`manifest`/`index`), `group` (= `sha256(run_id + group_label)[:16]`), `group_index`, and a free-form `variant_meta` blob. **Default role is `ancillary`. Executors must opt in to `variant`. Fail closed.**
  rationale: heterogeneous outputs (4 candidates + grid + manifest) cannot accidentally poison the variant group; executors that produce siblings declare them explicitly.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-014: Selection state lives at the thread, not the artifact. An append-only `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/selections.jsonl` records each `{ts, group, kept[], discarded[], by, note?}` event. Never mutated. Current-keepers reduces over the log
  rationale: handles partial selection, deselection, and revision without losing history; concurrent picks are safe (last write wins on read).
  load_bearing: True
- SD-015: `chosen_from_groups: [{group, sha256}]` on a consuming run is a **separate edge** from `parent_run_ids`. The DAG distinguishes "descended from X" (causal) from "picked over its siblings" (curatorial). The iteration video needs both
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-016: Denormalized `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/groups.json` index gives O(1) lookups for "what variants for run #N, which kept, which descended." Updated on run-write and selection-write
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-017: Agent gesture surface for variants — exactly five commands, one of which is mandatory-per-attempt:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-018: Runner-emitted prefix lines on every `executors run` and `orchestrators run` invocation, written to stdout BEFORE the rest of the command output (so the agent sees them in tool result):
  rationale: the agent's working memory is the previous tool's stdout; thread state must be in that stream every turn.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-019: Provenance block in `hype.metadata.json` (added to `pipeline` block by `builtin.cut`). Carries `{thread_id, thread_label (denormalized), run_id, parent_run_ids[], chosen_from_groups[], contributing_runs[{run_id, thread_id, artifact_path, sha256}], starred, agent_version}`. Denormalization of `thread_label` and `agent_version` makes the artifact self-contained after `rm -rf .artagents/`
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-020: `builtin.iteration_video` is a single orchestrator polymorphic across modalities, not per-modality orchestrators. Real threads are heterogeneous (storyboard → animation, music video) and the agent shouldn't have to pick a modality before knowing what's in the thread
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-021: Iteration-video executor chain: `iteration.collect` → `iteration.summarize` (calls `builtin.understand` in parallel) → `iteration.score` → `iteration.assemble` → `builtin.cut` → `builtin.render`. Three new executors; the rest are reused. `iteration.assemble` is the only piece with non-trivial new visual logic
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-022: Iteration-video outputs (a single variant group):
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-023: Default ancestry is `provenance-graph` (walk `parent_run_ids` backward from target), not `thread`. Threads are a human construct that drift; causal parentage is hash-derived and doesn't lie. The HTML report labels which runs were "in-thread" vs "pulled in by ancestry."
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-024: Quality floor: `iteration.collect` computes a `data_quality` score in [0,1]. If below `quality_floor` (default 0.6), the orchestrator **refuses to render** and emits an actionable report listing the specific runs missing `parent_run_ids` with exact backfill commands. `--force` bypasses, logged into provenance
  rationale: silently rendering a video that misorders or omits half the runs destroys trust permanently. Refusal must be a helpful editor, not a bureaucrat.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-025: `ModalityRenderer` registry at `artagents/modalities/` (sibling to `elements/`, `executors/`, `orchestrators/`). Each renderer is a small declarative file declaring `kinds`, `clip_modes`, `default_clip_mode_for(shape, style)`, `produces_audio`, `cost_hint`. Discoverable via `python3 -m artagents modalities {list, inspect}`
  rationale: replaces a hardcoded global decision table that would become unmaintainable as modalities multiply. Each renderer owns its own scoped logic.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-026: Capability declarations on artifacts: extend `output_artifacts` with `preview_modes: [...]` and `duration` (where applicable). Producers declare what previews are tractable. The renderer registry resolves `(kind, preview_modes)` to a renderer at assembly time
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-027: Agent surface for iteration video — five flags + one inspect command total:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-028: Audio-bed automatic selection: if `produces_audio` renderers cover >40% of clip duration → iterations-as-bed (cross-fade between audio variants). Else theme-declared bed. Else silence + subtle room tone. **Never generative music** — ages badly, fights the content
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-029: `generic_card` renderer is always registered as a fallback. When it fires, every iteration that uses it gets a "no renderer for `kind:<X>`" annotation in the HTML report and a stdout warning. Unknown modalities degrade gracefully and **loudly**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-030: Single chokepoint integration: `run_executor()` at `artagents/executors/runner.py:75` and the orchestrator-runner equivalent are wrapped with `threads.begin(request)` / `threads.finalize(record_id, result)`. The wrapper is a no-op when: `dry_run=True`, `request.out` is unwritable or under `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `request.thread == "@none"`, or env `ARTAGENTS_THREADS_OFF=1` is set. **No executor's `run.py` is modified except where it produces variant outputs.**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-031: Existing-executor patches required by this layer:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-032: Hashing strategy: `xxhash` for `inputs_digest` (fast, non-cryptographic, used for dedup detection only). `sha256` for `output_artifacts[*].sha256` (one-shot at run end, never blocking the runner mid-run). Multi-GB renders must not block
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-033: In-flight reaper: any run start scans `runs/*/run.json` for records with `ended_at: null` whose owning process is gone (PID stamped at begin). Marks them `returncode: -1, ended_at: <now>, status: "orphaned"`. Lazy, runs at most once per process
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-034: Backwards compatibility is mandatory. Existing `runs/*/` directories without `run.json` continue to work unmodified. `python3 -m artagents thread backfill` scans, computes hashes, and adopts orphan dirs into auto-named threads (clustered by hash-graph connected components, not mtime). All existing tests must pass without modification
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-035: Sprint phasing constraints (load-bearing for the planner):
  rationale:

- SD-036: Sprint cuts (explicitly out of scope for the 2-week sprint, deferred to follow-up):

- SD-038: Documentation deliverables for week-1 ship: `docs/threads.md` (one global doc explaining the model), one paragraph appended to `SKILL.md` instructing agents to run `thread show @active` at session start, footer line in `executors inspect` / `orchestrators inspect` output naming the active thread. **No per-tool `STAGE.md` is modified.**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-039: Schema versioning: `run.json`, `threads.json`, `selections.jsonl`, `groups.json`, and the `provenance` block all carry `schema_version: int`. Readers accept current and N-1; writers always write current; one-time migration runs on first read at upgrade time, with `.bak`
  rationale:

- SD-040: All paths in persisted JSON are repo-relative or content-addressed. No absolute paths. This makes thread export/sharing (a future feature) work for free as long as we hold the line now

- ADDITIONAL GAPS (orchestrator review of plan_v1.md). Treat each as required for v2:

1) Day 3 is overpacked. Auto-attribute (5-branch decision per SD-006 including lineage inference), prefix lines (SD-018), 5 CLI subcommands (thread new/list/show/archive/reopen), lifecycle (SD-007), and lazy reaper (SD-033) is realistically 8-10 hours of focused work. The only buffer is Day 10 shared with dogfood. Either (a) move the lazy reaper and one CLI subcommand (archive/reopen) to Day 4 morning, or (b) explicitly mark Day 3 as a 'risk day' with a named cut-list if it slips past 6pm.

2) Documentation timing is wrong in Step 4. SKILL.md paragraph + 'executors inspect' / 'orchestrators inspect' footer (SD-038) are scheduled for Day 5, but agents will start seeing the [thread] prefix on Day 3. The footer and SKILL.md paragraph must land Day 3 alongside the prefix lines so an agent reading tool output on Day 3 has docs that explain what they're seeing. Only docs/threads.md (the longer reference) belongs Day 5.

3) Add a 'Frozen Schema Review' checkpoint at end-of-Day-2. Once SD-008 fields ship, any change requires SD-039 migration support. The plan should make this an explicit milestone (literally a line in Day 2 acceptance: 'schema_version=1 frozen; any later change requires migration helper + .bak rotation test added before the change merges').

4) _run_upload_youtube bypass at artagents/executors/runner.py:78 short-circuits _run_executor_inner. SD-030's 'no-op when out is unwritable' covers it but the integration test plan must include a test that confirms upload.youtube produces zero thread artifacts and zero errors.

5) Nested-executor env threading is real plumbing not scheduled. SD-030 says 'children skip begin if ARTAGENTS_THREAD_ID env is set'. This requires modifying _run_external_executor's subprocess env at runner.py:258 to thread ARTAGENTS_THREAD_ID through. Schedule on Day 3 (alongside the wrapper expansion) and add a test in tests/test_threads_nested.py that verifies parent->child inheritance.

6) Secret/env-var redaction in cli_args_redacted (SD-008) needs a Day 2 scrub even before SD-041's broader privacy work lands. Basic rule: any CLI arg whose value matches an env-var-style pattern containing KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD gets the value replaced with '***REDACTED***'. Schedule as a 30-min Day 2 task with a unit test.

7) The Risks section is too generic. For each named risk add a one-line concrete mitigation. Specifically: 'Lock contention' -> 'fcntl 30s timeout, error message points at thread gc --force-unlock command'; 'builtin.understand rate limits' -> 'ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers configurable via env var ARTAGENTS_SUMMARIZE_CONCURRENCY default 4, with exponential backoff per call'; 'Schema bug post-Day-2' -> 'SD-039 migration helper added before any field change; .bak rotation test required'.

8) Add a Day 10 'demo milestone' as an acceptance criterion. Not just 'render works' but 'produce a 60-second iteration video against runs/artagents_logo_v3, screen-share it, manual checklist signed off'. The dogfood is the demo.

These are additive to the gate's 3 items already being addressed in revise. Land all 8 (gate's 3 + these 5 not already overlapping) before finalize.
- AGENT UX LAYER GAPS (orchestrator review). The plan currently treats agent UX as deliverables-to-land rather than a UX surface to design. Add an explicit '## Agent UX Surface' subsection to the sprint plan with day-tagged commitments addressing all of the following:

1) TIERED NOTICE/WARN DISCIPLINE. SD-018 names three tiers (info / notice / warn) but the plan must commit to firing rules: Info = every run; Notice = first run of process, gap >1h, cwd change, auto-reopen of archived thread; Warn = brief-novelty against thread history (parsable, rare). Acceptance criterion: 'Warn tier fires <5% of runs in dogfood or the trigger thresholds get tuned before Day 10.' Without this discipline the implementation drifts into warning-spam and agents learn to ignore the lines.

2) [HINT] LINE for suspected manual fan-out (3+ sequential runs of the same executor with no --variants flag) suggesting 'thread group <ids>'. Schedule on Day 4 alongside the [variants] nag. Soft nudge, not warning.

3) [THREAD-HEALTH] SMELL LINE on 'thread list' output (e.g., '12 variant groups, 0 kept' or '3 open threads idle >5d'). Schedule Day 3 with the lifecycle CLI.

4) SKILL.MD ONE-SENTENCE WORDING IS LOAD-BEARING. Every agent will pattern off it. The plan must specify the exact text to land on Day 3, not 'add a paragraph'. Suggested anchor: 'At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new.' Plan can refine but must commit to the exact wording.

5) OUTPUT-FORMAT STABILITY COMMITMENT. The [thread] and [variants] prefix lines are part of the public CLI contract. Add to Definition of Done: 'prefix line format governed by schema_version; format changes require a major version bump and a transition period.' Agents that pattern-match break silently otherwise.

6) LINE-ORDERING RULE when [thread], [variants], Notice, and Warn all fire on the same run. Specify: stream (stdout for all, before any other output); order (thread, variants, notice, warn, then command output); separator (single blank line between prefix block and command output). Trivial to specify on Day 2, expensive to fix later.

7) ITERATION_VIDEO INSPECT AS PRIMARY DISCOVERY TOOL. The plan treats it as one subcommand among five but it is THE gesture an agent should run before any iteration-video render (per the design's agent-UX reasoning). The SKILL.md text or a separate iteration-video doc must instruct: 'Always run iteration_video inspect <thread> before iteration_video run; it shows detected modalities, chosen renderers, estimated cost, and quality score so you can adjust before committing to a render.'

8) COST ESTIMATE SURFACING per SD-043. iteration_video inspect must print estimated cost (= summarize_calls * model_cost + render_cost_estimate) BEFORE the agent commits to a render. Schedule on Day 6 with iteration.collect (which has the run count) or Day 9 with the orchestrator wiring. Acceptance: 'inspect output includes a Cost section with low/high range and a one-line recommendation.'

9) THE FAILURE-MODE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (most important). An agent that forgets threads exist will silently lump everything into one giant pile and the killer demo dies. Add to Day 10 dogfood acceptance: 'verify that during dogfood the [thread] prefix appeared on the stdout of every executors run / orchestrators run invocation, that thread show @active was called by the agent before iteration_video, and that no run was attributed to thread @active when a more recent thread had been opened (lineage inference worked).' Make it observable, not assumed.

10) DOCUMENT WHEN EACH TIER FIRES in docs/threads.md so agents reading the doc can predict what they'll see. Day 5 deliverable, scoped to one short table.

These items are load-bearing for adoption: if the agent UX is sloppy, the data the iteration video reads is sloppy, and the demo lies. They are not deferrable to a follow-up sprint.
- FINAL TIGHTENING NOTE before finalize. Eight surgical edits to plan v3. Each is a concrete plan-text change, not a directional nudge. Land all eight in v4.

1) DAY 3 OVERPACK + DOC TIMING (single fix). Day 3 is now larger than v1 (auto-attribute + prefix + tiered Notice/Warn + 5 CLI subcommands + lazy reaper + --no-content). Rebalance:
  - Move 'archive' and 'reopen' subcommands AND the lazy reaper from Day 3 -> Day 4 morning.
  - Move the SKILL.md paragraph, the 'executors inspect' / 'orchestrators inspect' footer, and a one-page docs/threads.md#what-the-prefix-means STUB (with the tier-fires table) from Day 5 -> Day 3, so agents on Day 3 see the [thread] prefix AND the docs that explain it on the same day.
  - Day 5 keeps docs/threads.md long-form reference (Privacy, Concurrent Selection, Deferred Features), brief snapshot, provenance, backfill.

2) LINE-ORDERING RULE. Add to Day 2 deliverables + acceptance: 'All prefix lines are written to stdout in this exact order before any other command output: [thread], then [variants] (when present), then any Notice line, then any Warn line, then a blank separator line, then command output.' Add tests/test_threads_prefix_ordering.py that synthesizes a run with all four lines firing and asserts the order.

3) FAILURE-MODE DOGFOOD ACCEPTANCE (most important). Add to Day 10 acceptance verbatim: 'During the dogfood render, capture stdout of every executors run / orchestrators run invocation. Assert observably: (a) every invocation emitted a [thread] prefix line on stdout BEFORE other output; (b) the prefix correctly identified the active thread by ULID; (c) lineage inference fired when any --brief / --asset / --video / --input arg pointed inside runs/<R>/; (d) the [variants] nag fired for the logo-candidate-producing run and was silenced after thread keep; (e) thread show @active was called by the operating agent before iteration_video. These are observable assertions written into the dogfood log, not subjective notes.'

4) EXACT SKILL.MD VERBATIM WORDING. Pin the sentence on Day 3, not Day 5. Plan must commit to landing this exact text (or a refined version via a one-line note in the plan): 'At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new to your next command. Selections are append-only; the most recent write is authoritative on read; prior selections are preserved as history but do not affect current keepers.' (Combines SKILL.md anchor + SD-042 last-write-wins in one paragraph the agent reads once and acts on.)

5) OUTPUT-FORMAT STABILITY in Definition of Done. Add clause (k): 'The prefix line format ([thread] / [variants] / Notice / Warn) is part of the public CLI contract. Format changes require a major schema_version bump and a transition period documented in docs/threads.md. The format is treated as load-bearing for agent compatibility.'

6) FROZEN-SCHEMA CHECKPOINT at end of Day 2. Add to Day 2 acceptance: 'schema_version=1 is frozen at end of Day 2. Any field addition / removal / rename to SD-008 fields after end-of-Day-2 requires shipping an SD-039 migration helper plus a .bak rotation test in the same PR. This checkpoint is enforced in PR review for the rest of the sprint.'

7) NESTED-EXECUTOR ENV THREADING explicit deliverable. Day 3 deliverables must name verbatim: 'Modify _run_external_executor at artagents/executors/runner.py:258 to thread ARTAGENTS_THREAD_ID into the subprocess env when present, so external executor processes inherit the parent thread without re-stamping.' Add tests/test_threads_nested_env.py asserting parent->child inheritance and skip-begin behavior when env is set.

8) TIER DISCIPLINE acceptance criterion on Day 10. Add: 'In the dogfood run plus a synthetic 50-run replay, the WARN tier fires on <=5% of executor/orchestrator invocations. If above 5%, the brief-novelty trigger threshold is tuned before sign-off. Notice tier has no rate cap but is logged for review.'

These are the final items. After v4 lands them, plan goes to finalize. Items not in this note ([hint] line for fan-out, [thread-health] smell line, demo screen-share framing) are accepted as deferred to execution-time judgment.

Prior doc imported via --from-doc:
docs/design-thread-layer.md
Imported decisions (from the source doc's ## Settled Decisions section): 40
Imported decision details:
- SD-001: Use the noun `thread` for a creative pursuit, not `workstream`/`session`/`pursuit`. The name appears in every `[thread]` prefix line and must match the creator's mental model
  rationale: chosen after explicit subagent debate; matches creator language ("pull on this thread"); short to type; the git overload is tolerable in the creative-tools domain.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-002: Tags-not-folders: every run writes a `runs/<slug>/run.json` with a `thread_id` field. The `runs/` directory stays flat. Re-grouping (split/merge/attach) is a metadata edit, never a `mv` operation
  rationale: coupling physical layout to logical grouping makes re-attribution destructive and breaks path references in older timelines. Identity is by ULID, never by path.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-003: A single index file `.artagents/threads.json` holds the thread map and `active_thread_id` pointer. All updates go through `fcntl.flock` on a sidecar lock file plus atomic write (tmp + fsync + `os.replace`), with a rotated `.bak`
  rationale: parallel runs must not lose updates; the index is small enough that single-file is correct.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-004: IDs are 26-char Crockford ULIDs (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `group_id`), monotonic within a process. References between records are always by ULID, never by path or label
  rationale: lex-sortable, stable across renames, no central registry needed.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-005: `parent_run_ids` on a run is **plural and causal**, derived from input-artifact hashes against producer `run_id`s — not the temporal previous run in the thread. A run with no consumed artifacts has empty `parent_run_ids` (it is a root)
  rationale: temporal parentage lies during interleaved work; causal parentage is reconstructible and honest.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-006: Auto-attribute decision function, evaluated at run start under the lock:
  rationale: lineage inference is the highest-ROI auto-attribution improvement; it removes a whole class of mis-grouping when the agent works across shells.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-007: Thread lifecycle: `open → archived → (re)open`. Archive triggers are explicit command, successful export/publish, or idle ≥ `IDLE_ARCHIVE_WINDOW` (default 7d). Reopen triggers are explicit command or new run within `IDLE_REOPEN_WINDOW`. Lazy enforcement on read; no daemon
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-008: `run.json` schema (frozen for v1 of the layer). Required fields:
  rationale: this is the irreversible part. Every run produced after sprint day 1 either has these fields or doesn't, forever. Metadata can be collected now and used by deferred features later.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-009: Brief snapshotting: every run writes `runs/<slug>/brief.copy.txt` and stamps `brief_content_sha256` in `run.json`. Briefs get edited in place between runs; without snapshotting, prompt diffs in the iteration video are unreconstructable
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-010: `external_service_calls` captures `model` and `model_version` per call, plus `seed`, `cost_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `request_id` where available. Models drift (gpt-image-1 → gpt-image-2 produces different outputs); `agent_version` (toolkit git sha) is insufficient on its own. `request_id` lets deleted external artifacts be re-fetched
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-011: `input_artifacts` records `produced_by_run_id` at the moment of consumption (computed from artifact sha256 against known runs). Without this, the causal DAG must be reconstructed later from hashes — possible but expensive and broken if intermediate runs are deleted
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-012: `host_id` = `sha256(hostname:user)[:16]`. Captured per run for provenance only. Not used for tracking, not transmitted. Lets a future sync tool reconcile cross-machine threads
  rationale: cheap to capture, expensive to add later if missed.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-013: Variants primitive: extend each `output_artifact` with `role` (`variant`/`ancillary`/`manifest`/`index`), `group` (= `sha256(run_id + group_label)[:16]`), `group_index`, and a free-form `variant_meta` blob. **Default role is `ancillary`. Executors must opt in to `variant`. Fail closed.**
  rationale: heterogeneous outputs (4 candidates + grid + manifest) cannot accidentally poison the variant group; executors that produce siblings declare them explicitly.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-014: Selection state lives at the thread, not the artifact. An append-only `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/selections.jsonl` records each `{ts, group, kept[], discarded[], by, note?}` event. Never mutated. Current-keepers reduces over the log
  rationale: handles partial selection, deselection, and revision without losing history; concurrent picks are safe (last write wins on read).
  load_bearing: True
- SD-015: `chosen_from_groups: [{group, sha256}]` on a consuming run is a **separate edge** from `parent_run_ids`. The DAG distinguishes "descended from X" (causal) from "picked over its siblings" (curatorial). The iteration video needs both
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-016: Denormalized `.artagents/threads/<thread-id>/groups.json` index gives O(1) lookups for "what variants for run #N, which kept, which descended." Updated on run-write and selection-write
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-017: Agent gesture surface for variants — exactly five commands, one of which is mandatory-per-attempt:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-018: Runner-emitted prefix lines on every `executors run` and `orchestrators run` invocation, written to stdout BEFORE the rest of the command output (so the agent sees them in tool result):
  rationale: the agent's working memory is the previous tool's stdout; thread state must be in that stream every turn.
  load_bearing: False
- SD-019: Provenance block in `hype.metadata.json` (added to `pipeline` block by `builtin.cut`). Carries `{thread_id, thread_label (denormalized), run_id, parent_run_ids[], chosen_from_groups[], contributing_runs[{run_id, thread_id, artifact_path, sha256}], starred, agent_version}`. Denormalization of `thread_label` and `agent_version` makes the artifact self-contained after `rm -rf .artagents/`
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-020: `builtin.iteration_video` is a single orchestrator polymorphic across modalities, not per-modality orchestrators. Real threads are heterogeneous (storyboard → animation, music video) and the agent shouldn't have to pick a modality before knowing what's in the thread
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-021: Iteration-video executor chain: `iteration.collect` → `iteration.summarize` (calls `builtin.understand` in parallel) → `iteration.score` → `iteration.assemble` → `builtin.cut` → `builtin.render`. Three new executors; the rest are reused. `iteration.assemble` is the only piece with non-trivial new visual logic
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-022: Iteration-video outputs (a single variant group):
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-023: Default ancestry is `provenance-graph` (walk `parent_run_ids` backward from target), not `thread`. Threads are a human construct that drift; causal parentage is hash-derived and doesn't lie. The HTML report labels which runs were "in-thread" vs "pulled in by ancestry."
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-024: Quality floor: `iteration.collect` computes a `data_quality` score in [0,1]. If below `quality_floor` (default 0.6), the orchestrator **refuses to render** and emits an actionable report listing the specific runs missing `parent_run_ids` with exact backfill commands. `--force` bypasses, logged into provenance
  rationale: silently rendering a video that misorders or omits half the runs destroys trust permanently. Refusal must be a helpful editor, not a bureaucrat.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-025: `ModalityRenderer` registry at `artagents/modalities/` (sibling to `elements/`, `executors/`, `orchestrators/`). Each renderer is a small declarative file declaring `kinds`, `clip_modes`, `default_clip_mode_for(shape, style)`, `produces_audio`, `cost_hint`. Discoverable via `python3 -m artagents modalities {list, inspect}`
  rationale: replaces a hardcoded global decision table that would become unmaintainable as modalities multiply. Each renderer owns its own scoped logic.
  load_bearing: True
- SD-026: Capability declarations on artifacts: extend `output_artifacts` with `preview_modes: [...]` and `duration` (where applicable). Producers declare what previews are tractable. The renderer registry resolves `(kind, preview_modes)` to a renderer at assembly time
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-027: Agent surface for iteration video — five flags + one inspect command total:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-028: Audio-bed automatic selection: if `produces_audio` renderers cover >40% of clip duration → iterations-as-bed (cross-fade between audio variants). Else theme-declared bed. Else silence + subtle room tone. **Never generative music** — ages badly, fights the content
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-029: `generic_card` renderer is always registered as a fallback. When it fires, every iteration that uses it gets a "no renderer for `kind:<X>`" annotation in the HTML report and a stdout warning. Unknown modalities degrade gracefully and **loudly**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-030: Single chokepoint integration: `run_executor()` at `artagents/executors/runner.py:75` and the orchestrator-runner equivalent are wrapped with `threads.begin(request)` / `threads.finalize(record_id, result)`. The wrapper is a no-op when: `dry_run=True`, `request.out` is unwritable or under `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `request.thread == "@none"`, or env `ARTAGENTS_THREADS_OFF=1` is set. **No executor's `run.py` is modified except where it produces variant outputs.**
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-031: Existing-executor patches required by this layer:
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: False
- SD-032: Hashing strategy: `xxhash` for `inputs_digest` (fast, non-cryptographic, used for dedup detection only). `sha256` for `output_artifacts[*].sha256` (one-shot at run end, never blocking the runner mid-run). Multi-GB renders must not block
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-033: In-flight reaper: any run start scans `runs/*/run.json` for records with `ended_at: null` whose owning process is gone (PID stamped at begin). Marks them `returncode: -1, ended_at: <now>, status: "orphaned"`. Lazy, runs at most once per process
  rationale: 
  load_bearing: True
- SD-034: Backwards compatibility is mandatory. Existing `runs/*/` directories without `run.json` continue to work unmodified. `python3 -m artagents thread backfill` scans, computes hashes, and adopts orphan dirs into auto-named threads (clustered by hash-graph connected components, not mtime). All existing tests must pass without modification

- SD-035: Sprint phasing constraints (load-bearing for the planner):

  rationale:

- SD-039: Schema versioning: `run.json`, `threads.json`, `selections.jsonl`, `groups.json`, and the `provenance` block all carry `schema_version: int`. Readers accept current and N-1; writers always write current; one-time migration runs on first read at upgrade time, with `.bak`
  rationale:

- SD-040: All paths in persisted JSON are repo-relative or content-addressed. No absolute paths. This makes thread export/sharing (a future feature) work for free as long as we hold the line now

There is no Warn brief-novelty trigger in v1.\n+\n+Acceptance: tests cover each Notice trigger, and dogfood logs are reviewable for Notice frequency without enforcing a Warn-rate metric.\n+\n+### UX-3: Variant Nag Discipline\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 4 implementation; Day 5 docs.\n+\n+`[variants]` appears only when a run produced unresolved variants. It points to the required keep/dismiss gesture and is silenced by `thread keep <run-id>:<n>[,<n>]` or `thread keep <run-id>:none`.\n+\n+Acceptance: Day 10 dogfood verifies the logo-candidate-producing run emitted `[variants]` and that the line disappeared after `thread keep`.\n+\n+### UX-4: SKILL.md Exact Wording\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 3.\n+\n+The sprint commits to this exact paragraph in `SKILL.md`:\n+\n+> At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new to your next command. Selections are append-only; the most recent write is authoritative on read; prior selections are preserved as history but do not affect current keepers.\n+\n+Refinements during the sprint require an explicit plan update because agents will pattern-match this text.\n+\n+Acceptance: `tests/test_threads_skill_md_text.py` asserts the exact paragraph.\n+\n+### UX-5: Output-Format Stability\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 2 contract; Day 3 implementation; Definition of Done.\n+\n+The v1 prefix formats `[thread]`, `[variants]`, and `Notice:` are public CLI contract. `schema_version` governs the format. Any format change requires a major `schema_version` bump and a transition period documented in `docs/threads.md`.\n+\n+Acceptance: the Definition of Done treats prefix format as load-bearing for agent compatibility.\n+\n+### UX-6: Line Ordering\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 2 contract; Day 3 implementation; Day 5 docs.\n+\n+All prefix lines are written to stdout before any other command output. V1 order is:\n+\n+```text\n+[thread]\n+[variants]  # only when present\n+Notice:     # only when present\n+\n+command output\n+```\n+\n+There is one blank separator line between the prefix block and command output.\n+\n+Acceptance: `tests/test_threads_line_ordering.py` synthesizes a run where all v1 prefix lines fire and asserts stdout order.\n+\n+### UX-7: Inspect Before Render\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 3 SKILL/docs note; Day 5 `docs/threads.md`; Day 9 command implementation.\n+\n+Agents must run `iteration_video inspect <thread>` before `iteration_video` render. Inspect is the discovery gesture: it shows detected modalities, chosen renderers, quality score, cache counts, and estimated cost before render work begins.\n+\n+Acceptance: Day 10 dogfood log proves `thread show @active` and `iteration_video inspect <thread>` were called before render.\n+\n+### UX-8: Cost Estimate\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 9.\n+\n+`iteration_video inspect <thread>` prints a single v1 Cost line before render:\n+\n+```text\n+Estimated cost: ~$0.42 (47 calls x $0.009)\n+```\n+\n+No low/high range and no recommendation enum ship in v1 per DEF-9.\n+\n+Acceptance: `tests/test_iteration_video_inspect.py` asserts the single-number Cost line and verifies inspect does not render or dispatch `builtin.understand`.\n+\n+### UX-9: Failure-Mode Dogfood Acceptance\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 10.\n+\n+The primary UX failure mode is silent misattribution. Dogfood must make attribution observable, not assumed.\n+\n+Acceptance: `tests/test_dogfood_failure_modes.py` replays the dogfood transcript and verifies `[thread]` prefix coverage, active-thread ULID correctness, lineage inference for `runs/<R>/` input args, `[variants]` nag/silence behavior, and pre-render `thread show @active`.\n+\n+### UX-10: Tier Firing Table\n+\n+**Day tag:** Day 5.\n+\n+`docs/threads.md` includes a short v1 table mapping surface to trigger and example:\n+\n+- `[thread]`: every eligible executor/orchestrator run.\n+- `[variants]`: unresolved variant group exists.\n+- `Notice:`: first run of process, gap greater than 1 hour, cwd change, or auto-reopen.\n+\n+Acceptance: `tests/test_threads_md_sections.py` checks that the table exists and does not document deferred `[hint]`, `[thread-health]`, or Warn brief-novelty behavior as v1 features.\n*** End Patch\n"

2) LINE-ORDERING RULE. Add to Day 2 deliverables + acceptance: 'All prefix lines are written to stdout in this exact order before any other command output: [thread], then [variants] (when present), then any Notice line, then any Warn line, then a blank separator line, then command output.' Add tests/test_threads_prefix_ordering.py that synthesizes a run with all four lines firing and asserts the order.

3) FAILURE-MODE DOGFOOD ACCEPTANCE (most important). Add to Day 10 acceptance verbatim: 'During the dogfood render, capture stdout of every executors run / orchestrators run invocation. Assert observably: (a) every invocation emitted a [thread] prefix line on stdout BEFORE other output; (b) the prefix correctly identified the active thread by ULID; (c) lineage inference fired when any --brief / --asset / --video / --input arg pointed inside runs/<R>/; (d) the [variants] nag fired for the logo-candidate-producing run and was silenced after thread keep; (e) thread show @active was called by the operating agent before iteration_video. These are observable assertions written into the dogfood log, not subjective notes.'

4) EXACT SKILL.MD VERBATIM WORDING. Pin the sentence on Day 3, not Day 5. Plan must commit to landing this exact text (or a refined version via a one-line note in the plan): 'At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new to your next command. Selections are append-only; the most recent write is authoritative on read; prior selections are preserved as history but do not affect current keepers.' (Combines SKILL.md anchor + SD-042 last-write-wins in one paragraph the agent reads once and acts on.)

Format changes require a major schema_version bump and a transition period documented in docs/threads.md. The format is treated as load-bearing for agent compatibility.'

Any field addition / removal / rename to SD-008 fields after end-of-Day-2 requires shipping an SD-039 migration helper plus a .bak rotation test in the same PR. This checkpoint is enforced in PR review for the rest of the sprint.'

If above 5%, the brief-novelty trigger threshold is tuned before sign-off. Notice tier has no rate cap but is logged for review.'
